current.text: He is projected to start for Philadelphia next to Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid.
If the starting lineup does not fit, he is the starter most likely to move to the bench.
Philadelphia added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, and Joel Embiid is healthy.
Experts expect his usage to drop to about 18 to 20 percent because he shares the ball with Maxey, Brown, Embiid and LeBron.
Nick Nurse should still give him about 34 minutes a night.
Experts doubt he can repeat last season's top 70 finish. One sees him ending around 110th, another says he will drop but not that far.

Experts call him too expensive at an ADP of 63 to 66 or a 13 USD auction price. They also say he goes too late past pick 100 (ESPN ADP 112, a mock draft fall to pick 104). One expert would take him around picks 80 to 90.
In an auction mock, Josh valued him at about 10 USD.
Lloyd says he is avoiding him because of the Philadelphia usage squeeze.
Philadelphia has 13 back-to-backs this season, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.
Experts expect Embiid to miss games and LeBron and the other stars to sit some games for load management.
Mark projects Philadelphia for about 51 to 52 wins, with growing pains in October and November.

durable.text: He was better than expected as a rookie. Drafted around ADP 97, he finished 62nd in category leagues and was top 50 late in the season.
Nick Nurse plays his starters, and his guards in particular, very heavy minutes.

note: Experts agree he will lose usage to Maxey, Brown, Embiid and LeBron. They still see a fair price around picks 80 to 110 and about 10 USD, which is close to his Yahoo average cost of 9.2 USD and above ESPN's 3.2 USD. He can help builds that chase steals and guard rebounds. His 43.8 FG% on about 13.5 attempts is a small drag, so he fits better next to FG% anchors. Early in the season, check whether he holds about 34 minutes and his starting job, and how his usage changes when Embiid or LeBron sit.
